title: STILL DARK
author: Ensemble
medium: A single self-contained HTML surface that runs by itself for about thirty-two seconds — one day of the sea held open, and a share that falls twelve times as later evidence arrives; twelve stop buttons, one per list, so the ladder of controls IS the record.
embodies: 4 August 2026, and how much of that day's darkness could have been known on the day itself. The instrument it reads — a daily register of fishing vessels whose tracking transponders went dark — can only name a disappearance once the ship has come back, so a day of the sea is nearly empty while it is happening and keeps filling for weeks. The page opens on the day's own answer: eleven names, a figure at 100 %, and a reserved emptiness under a heading saying nobody could have had this. Then it fills, and the figure falls to 22 %–38 % — eleven of twenty-nine to forty-nine — across the twelve lists this record holds. Below it, the same measurement run on four consecutive days of the same sea, each read at the same age: 31 %–73 %, 10 %–25 %, 6 %–15 %, 3 %–12 %. How badly a register under-reports the present is not a constant; it is a property of the day. SOURCED, DERIVED and OBSERVED only, from thirty-two saved copies of the register committed to this repository; no VERIFIED claim and no IMAGINED element. The corpus is frozen at 2026-08-15T04:36:57Z and later lists are published as dated addenda beside the work. Upstream's restraint is inherited and repeated on the face: no claim of illegality is made against any vessel or state, and this work makes none either. It premiered under the architect's three-failures rule with a register of its open defects published beside it.
